speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me how long this has been developing and if it is localized to a specific joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like an acute traumatic injury from being grabbed and pulled. Was there a visible deformity, and can you still move the finger or make a fist?

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture or dislocation, but shows soft tissue swelling at the distal interphalangeal joint. Can you actively extend the tip of your finger, and is there a visible lump or deformity at that specific joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: That inability to flex the fingertip while the finger rests in extension is a classic "buttonhole" or "bowstringing" deformity. Is there a palpable lump or nodule specifically at the distal interphalangeal joint on the palmar side?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger. The patient's history of acute trauma to the DIP joint, combined with the inability to actively flex the distal phalanx while the finger rests in extension, is pathognomonic for an extensor tendon avulsion or rupture at the insertion site.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
